classification.habitat: Dry open ground, roadsides, wastelands and sandy soils
classification.distribution: Widely distributed across India and many warm regions of the world

identification.description: A low-growing herb with opposite compound leaves and distinctive hard, spiny fruits.
identification.whole_plant: Prostrate, spreading herb forming mats on open ground.
identification.root: Slender branched root system; authenticate medicinal root material before use.
identification.stem: Trailing, branched stems, often hairy and close to the ground.
identification.leaf: Opposite, pinnate leaves with small paired leaflets; leaflets are unequal in size within a leaf pair.
identification.flower: Small solitary yellow flowers borne in leaf axils.
identification.fruit: Characteristic hard, globose to angled schizocarp with sharp spines; the spiny fruit is a key field character.
identification.seed: Seeds are enclosed within the hard segments of the spiny fruit.
identification.bark: Not applicable as a distinct medicinal bark character for the herb.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Tribulus contains steroidal saponins and other secondary metabolites reported in different plant parts; constituent profiles vary with plant material and geography, so exact composition should be source-verified.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Tribulus terrestris is widely studied as a botanical used traditionally for urinary and reproductive-system indications. Modern evidence should not be presented as proof of clinical efficacy without condition-specific clinical evidence.
modern_information.safety_notes: Confirm species and plant part; avoid treating traditional indications as a substitute for diagnosis or evidence-based treatment.

mnemonics: Gokshura = go-like thorn: remember the conspicuously spiny fruit.
student.quick_revision: Gokshura (Tribulus terrestris) is a low-growing Zygophyllaceae herb distinguished by its yellow flowers and hard spiny fruits; the project record lists fruit as useful.

teaching_points: Use the spiny fruit to demonstrate diagnostic field identification.
Discuss the importance of distinguishing Tribulus from other plants sold under vernacular names such as gokhru.
discussion_points: Traditional urinary indications versus modern evidence
Botanical authentication of commercially supplied crude drug
practical_points: Observe habit, leaflets, flower and especially fruit spines.
Document specimen source and authentication status in practical records.
